issues: “The queen” is clearly the queen of Lamoni from the preceding scene, but the scene does not specify the room or precise setting. The king’s body and sepulchre preparation are supported; do not depict the burial as completed.

“Ammon” and “the queen” are not expressly named in every fact, but identity carries over from the preceding scene. Narration and quoted dialogue stay within supplied verses; the servants’ report and disagreement are rightly treated as reported speech.

The scene gives no exact place or posture for the king. The account supports Ammon entering, seeing him, and knowing he is not dead, but not a particular bed, visible spiritual effect, or the queen’s presence.
The man Ammon discusses is Lamoni in context, but the text does not specify whether he is visible during the conversation. Keep the future rising as prediction, not an event in this scene.
The bed is explicit, but the queen’s remaining beside it is an inference rather than a stated position; passage of time has no specified visual form.

The king’s rising and sinking and the queen’s sinking are explicit. The text does not explicitly say he rises from the bed, so show no more specific starting posture than the account supports; the Redeemer is testimony, not visibly present.
The text says three people sank, but does not identify the other two; the servants fall by the end of their calling on the Lord. Abish’s conversion vision is backstory, not a scene event.

The woman is identified as Abish in the preceding verse, but this verse calls her only “she.” Preserve the sequence: she first sees the prostrate group, then runs house to house; do not place that group among the houses.

The flock-scattering men rebuke the murmurers, but their physical presence at the king’s house is not specified. The first group’s claim in verse 19 is indirect reported speech, so avoid presenting the supplied paraphrase as verbatim dialogue.
The account supports the man raising his sword and falling dead, but does not state what causes the fall. Mosiah’s reported earlier assurance is not a present scene event; setting is unspecified.

The multitude’s competing claims are reported but not quoted verbatim in the scene. The woman servant’s arrival and sorrow are explicit; the precise setting and individual speakers remain unspecified.
Abish, the queen, and the hand-taking and rising are supported. The multitude’s presence follows from the preceding scene, but its reactions are unspecified.
The queen’s ununderstood words must not be invented or rendered as readable speech. Other listed characters are not stated to be present in this verse, though the preceding scene establishes a crowd.
Lamoni’s actions and the listeners’ belief or departure are supported. Exact teaching, crowd composition, and the specific location where people go are not supplied.
The reported testimony about seeing and conversing with angels is not a present angel appearance. The exact words of the witnesses and specific setting are unspecified.
Baptism and church establishment are explicit, but no setting, method, officiants, or church appearance is specified. The extended arm is figurative, not a visible divine arm.
